_about: The validations of a declared medallion flow (spec 3.8.1, 3.8.2) and of its design (D2 to D9), each naming the question it protects.

then.flag: a step of a medallion flow declares no step kind

rules.why: The kinds are the flow's vocabulary; a step without one cannot be checked against it (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: the step kind is not one of the medallion's: create_batch, check_sources_ready, copy_to_bronze, run_gate, build_reference, build_entity, build_output, reconcile, mark_validated

rules.why: A flow uses only the fixed kinds, so the implementation agent can emit every step from a template (spec 3.8.1, 3.8.2 Vocabulary).

then.flag: a run_gate step does not say which gate it runs (1, 2 or 3)

rules.why: Each gate runs at one boundary: 1 landing to bronze, 2 bronze to silver, 3 silver to gold (spec 3.7).

then.flag: the medallion flow has no create_batch step

rules.why: Exactly one create_batch per flow (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: the medallion flow has more than one create_batch step

rules.why: Exactly one create_batch per flow (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: the medallion flow has no check_sources_ready step

rules.why: Exactly one check_sources_ready per flow (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: the medallion flow has more than one check_sources_ready step

rules.why: Exactly one check_sources_ready per flow (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: the medallion flow has no mark_validated step

rules.why: Exactly one mark_validated per flow (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: the medallion flow has more than one mark_validated step

rules.why: Exactly one mark_validated per flow (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: the medallion flow has no step that runs gate 1

rules.why: Every gate runs exactly once per batch (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: the medallion flow has no step that runs gate 2

rules.why: Every gate runs exactly once per batch (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: the medallion flow has no step that runs gate 3

rules.why: Every gate runs exactly once per batch (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: two steps of the medallion flow run the same gate

rules.why: Every gate runs exactly once per batch (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: a check_sources_ready step does not come after create_batch

rules.why: The sources are checked for an open batch (spec 3.8.1, order 1-2).

then.flag: a copy_to_bronze step does not come after check_sources_ready

rules.why: A source is copied only when every expected source has rows for the period (spec 3.8.1, order 2-3).

then.flag: a run_gate step (gate 1) runs before a copy_to_bronze step has finished

rules.why: Gate 1 checks the whole of bronze, so it waits for every copy (spec 3.8.1, order 3-4).

then.flag: a build_reference step does not come after run_gate (gate 1)

rules.why: Reference data is built from a bronze that passed gate 1 (spec 3.8.1, order 4-5).

then.flag: a build_entity step does not come after run_gate (gate 1)

rules.why: A silver entity is built only from a bronze that passed gate 1 (spec 3.8.2 Gate placement).

then.flag: a run_gate step (gate 2) runs before a build_entity step has finished

rules.why: Gate 2 checks the whole of silver, so it waits for every entity (spec 3.8.1, order 6-7).

then.flag: a build_output step does not come after run_gate (gate 2)

rules.why: A gold output is built only from a silver that passed gate 2 (spec 3.8.2 Gate placement).

then.flag: a run_gate step (gate 3) runs before a build_output step has finished

rules.why: Gate 3 checks the whole of gold, so it waits for every output (spec 3.8.1, order 8-9).

then.flag: a reconcile step does not come after run_gate (gate 3)

rules.why: A gold total is reconciled once gold passed gate 3 (spec 3.8.1, order 9-10).

then.flag: a mark_validated step does not come after run_gate (gate 3)

rules.why: The batch is validated only after gate 3 (spec 3.8.2 Gate placement).

then.flag: a mark_validated step runs before a reconcile step has finished

rules.why: Every reconciliation has run before the batch is handed to approval (spec 3.8.1, order 10-11).

then.flag: the step reads gold and writes a lower layer

rules.why: Data moves up the layers, never down (spec 3.8.2 Layer direction).

then.flag: the step reads silver and writes bronze

rules.why: Data moves up the layers, never down (spec 3.8.2 Layer direction).

then.flag: a copy_to_bronze step writes outside bronze

rules.why: A copy lands one source in bronze, and nothing else (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: a build_entity step writes outside silver

rules.why: An entity is one silver table (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: a build_output step writes outside gold

rules.why: An output is one gold table (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: a build_output step reads a gold table

rules.why: An output reads silver; one output reading another is forbidden (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: a run_gate step writes a data layer

rules.why: A gate reads and records; it changes no data (spec 3.8.1).

then.flag: a field is both derived by a rule and fed by a column or field

rules.why: Exactly one of derived_by or fed_by: a field is either computed or copied (D4, D5).

then.flag: a rule reads a gold field to produce a bronze or silver one

rules.why: A rule's inputs sit in the same or a lower layer than its output (D6).

then.flag: a rule reads a silver field to produce a bronze one

rules.why: A rule's inputs sit in the same or a lower layer than its output (D6).

then.flag: an artifact of the flow sits in another layer than the dataset it represents

rules.why: The flow's tables are the design's datasets; one layer for both (D8).

then.flag: an artifact representing a source table is not in the source layer

rules.why: A source table is read from outside, before bronze (D2, D8).

then.flag: two steps execute the same copy policy, entity, output or rule

rules.why: Exactly one step executes a unit of transformation (D8 Single executor).

then.flag: a build_entity step does not write the dataset its entity is materialised as

rules.why: The step that builds an entity writes the entity's table (D4, D8).

then.flag: a build_output step does not write the dataset its output is materialised as

rules.why: The step that builds an output writes the output's table (D5, D8).

then.flag: a person has write access on silver

rules.why: No human identity writes silver or gold (D9).

then.flag: a person has write access on gold

rules.why: No human identity writes silver or gold (D9).

then.flag: a copy_to_bronze step executes a ConformedEntity or Output or DerivationRule

rules.why: A copy runs a copy policy, an entity step an entity and its rules, an output step an output and its rules (D8).

then.flag: a build_entity step executes a CopyPolicy or Output

rules.why: A copy runs a copy policy, an entity step an entity and its rules, an output step an output and its rules (D8).

then.flag: a build_output step executes a CopyPolicy or ConformedEntity

rules.why: A copy runs a copy policy, an entity step an entity and its rules, an output step an output and its rules (D8).

then.flag: a unit test is a test of something it cannot prove: it tests a derivation rule or a quality rule

rules.why: Each kind of test proves one kind of thing, so the build plan's tests are generated from it (D9).

then.flag: a contract test is a test of something it cannot prove: it tests an output

rules.why: Each kind of test proves one kind of thing, so the build plan's tests are generated from it (D9).

then.flag: a parity test is a test of something it cannot prove: it tests an output

rules.why: Each kind of test proves one kind of thing, so the build plan's tests are generated from it (D9).

then.flag: a flow test is a test of something it cannot prove: it tests a flow

rules.why: Each kind of test proves one kind of thing, so the build plan's tests are generated from it (D9).

then.flag: a forced failure test is a test of something it cannot prove: it tests a quality rule or a runbook

rules.why: Each kind of test proves one kind of thing, so the build plan's tests are generated from it (D9).

then.flag: the rule does not say what happens on tie

rules.why: The five standard edge cases are answered before a rule is complete (D6).

then.flag: the rule does not say what happens on null input

rules.why: The five standard edge cases are answered before a rule is complete (D6).

then.flag: the rule does not say what happens on missing history

rules.why: The five standard edge cases are answered before a rule is complete (D6).

then.flag: the rule does not say what happens on younger than lookback

rules.why: The five standard edge cases are answered before a rule is complete (D6).

then.flag: the rule does not say what happens on duplicate input

rules.why: The five standard edge cases are answered before a rule is complete (D6).
